rationale:
`assets/skills/habeas-bootstrap-requirements/SKILL.md` is a bundled skill, recognized by its front matter, so it is a site of `requirements.cli.skill_conventions.references`. The requirement lets a skill link to files for specialized material. It requires each such link to say when to read the file.

The file has one Markdown link, the `[CI example](../habeas/references/ci.md)` link in workflow step 9. The sentence around it gives the trigger. It says to recommend separate successful collection and `habeas coverage-check` steps in project CI, "using the Habeas CI example". The reader therefore knows to open the file when writing that CI recommendation, and I count that as saying when to read it.

The file also mentions `references/authoring-failures.md` and `references/fixme.md` of other skills, but only as backticked paths, not as links. Even so, each comes with its trigger. The first is read when `habeas author --stdout` fails. The second is read when the user defers a possible bug. There are no other links, and I found no unconditioned link, so the site meets the requirement.

The violation query listed no matches, so there were none to judge.
